pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all three seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ ' when starred. test 'AC-2' checks the exact list with one starred item.
The WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id query is covered by test 'AC-3'. It stars 3 and 1 in that order and expects id order in the result.
test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all against the full list in id order with the starred item marked.
The nav link is built per view. test 'AC-5' asserts the exact anchors on both views.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) returns 400 for anything else. test 'AC-6' covers 'Starred', 'none', empty and '__proto__', and checks there is no <li> in the body.

traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. test 'AC-7' asserts it. traffic/src/index.js requests each route string as `https://app.internal${path}`, so the query is kept. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts the query.

findings.what: AC-7 only checks that the route string is in routes.json. It does not check that the traffic Worker requests the query string.
findings.fix: Optionally add a traffic.test.js case asserting that the fake app sees '/?show=starred'.

lenses.note: The spec has an owner go dated 2026-10-12. The decisions (starred items keep their place; the view is a query parameter) are followed. The traffic-config-check loosening is needed to list the route.
All 7 acceptance items are named by tests. All four rows of the States table have a test. The spec file was added in the same commit as the code and was not edited afterwards.

The tests assert behaviour. I could not run them: `npm test` failed because vitest is not installed here. CI runs them. No tests were deleted. The fake app in traffic.test.js was widened to include the query string.
The README mentions ?show=starred. Nothing stale found.
Input validation uses hasOwn, so __proto__ and empty values return 400. The SQL is static, with no interpolation of user input.
The title is HTML-escaped. The `show` value is never echoed back or put into SQL. No instructions were planted in the repository content.
The diff changes only a minimal server-rendered HTML page. There are no UI or style files.
There is no browser flow or UI files to exercise; the page is minimal HTML covered by Worker tests.
The PR's claims match the diff: 400 on other values, the migration, the routes, the checker change and the test-fake change.
